title: steady-state-pipeline-probing-lab-diary
content:
Lab diary: steady-state pipeline probing (notes, micro-experiments, reproducible commands)

Summary / motivation:
- Observed a small but persistent periodic jitter in 99th percentile token latency across a fleet using flash-backed fused ops. Jitter shows up after warmup (steady-state), not during cold-start. We need to understand whether this is kernel-level (FlashAttention prefetch behavior), scheduler-level (coalescer wakeups/sleep cycles), or KV-cache / paged attention interactions.
- Goal: isolate root cause and find low-risk mitigations that don't regress throughput or token quality.

High-level hypothesis tree:
1) Kernel prefetch/resident-page churn: paged attention forces occasional page-in phases which increase single-token latency intermittently.
2) Scheduler/coalescer cadence: microbatch coalescer sleeps/flushes on heuristics that interact with sequence length distribution -> periodic flush boundaries.
3) Kernel handoff latency: fused-ops -> flashattention kernel handoffs create gaps when switching execution paths for certain seq-len/kv-cache states.
4) KV-cache backpressure: reads/writes to KV backend are serialized under high occupancy and manifest as tail events.

Quick checklist carried forward:
- Reproduce on single-device local rig with minimal filesystem noise.
- Capture 10k token-level traces with full per-kernel timestamps and queue lengths.
- Sweep coalescer thresholds, prefetch depth, and fusion disable flags.
- Run with and without paged attention enabled (flash vs paged).
- Correlate with GPU SM util + PCIe fault counters + host IO latencies.

Experiment 1: Baseline steady-state run (flash + fusedops enabled)
- Config: model=redwood-15B, seq-prefix=64, gen_len=512, token_rate=70 t/s, continuous stream of prompts (no idle).
- Runtime flags: --use-flashattention --enable-fused-ops --coalescer=auto --prefetch=on
- Observations: median per-token latency = 6.9 ms, p95 = 12.8 ms, p99 = 27.6 ms. Periodic spikes every ~120s, spike amplitude +80–110% of p99.
- Trace pattern: kernel A (fused matmul) -> kernel B (flash-attn) -> kernel C (kv-write) -> 200–400us pause -> kernel B resumes. Pause correlates with increased host-side page-ins reported by OS.

Experiment 2: Disable paged attention (force in-memory flash only)
- Flags: --force-no-paging --use-flashattention --enable-fused-ops
- Observations: median ~6.8 ms (unchanged), p95 ~12.4 ms (slight improvement), p99 ~18.2 ms (significant improvement). Periodic spikes largely gone.
- Interpretation: paging likely contributor. But cautions: test rig has roomy GPU memory; customer rigs with constrained memory may not be able to avoid paging.

Experiment 3: Toggle fused ops off
- Flags: --use-flashattention --disable-fused-ops
- Observations: median up to 7.5 ms (small regression), p99 reduced to ~16.5 ms relative to baseline. Spike cadence changed (more frequent but lower amplitude).
- Interpretation: fused ops introduce kernel handoffs that can amplify page-in stalls; without fusion we pay a small median cost but reduce extreme tails.

Experiment 4: Coalescer aggressive threshold (no sleep)
- Flags: --coalescer=aggressive --coalescer-sleep-ms=0 --prefetch=on
- Observations: throughput slightly decreased under light load; p99 improved modestly; spikes less periodic but still present. CPU wakeups increase.
- Tradeoffs: zero-sleep reduces cadence-induced flushes, but CPU overhead hurts multi-tenant hosts.

Detailed trace snippet (abridged):
- t=0 kernel: fused-gemm (12us) -> flash-attn (1.2ms) -> kv-write (18us) -> coalescer idles (180us) -> page-in stall detected (host 2.1ms) -> flash-attn resumes (980us) -> kv-write commit (30us) -> total token latency 5.8ms
- During spike: identical pattern but page-in stall ~11ms -> token latency 16.9ms

Metrics captured and how:
- kernel timeline: nvprof-like traces (timestamped per kernel).
- queue lengths: internal coalescer queue depth sampled per 10ms window.
- host IO: /proc/vmstat deltas, iostat for NVMe drops, dmesg for page-faults.
- GPU metrics: sm_util, dram_util, l2_hit_rate via nvidia-smi & CUPTI where available.

Repro commands (local test harness):
- ./run_inference_bench --model redwood-15B --threads 4 --seq-prefix 64 --gen-len 512 --rate 70 --duration 900 --tracing=kernel,timing,coalescer,host-io --flags "use_flashattention=true;enable_fused_ops=true;coalescer=auto;prefetch=on"
- collection: ./collect_traces.sh $(pidof run_inference_bench) /tmp/traces/run-$(date +%s)

Intermediate conclusions so far:
- Primary contributor to steady-state p99 seems to be intermittent paging activity in workloads where kernel execution path expects pages to be resident. Paged attention shows worst tails.
- Fused ops are amplifiers: they reduce median work but create larger contiguous kernel blocks that are more susceptible to a single page-in or IO hiccup (larger critical section).
- Coalescer heuristics interact with cadence; turning aggressive helps but is not net-positive for shared hosts.

Potential mitigations (ranked by risk):
1) Recommend default: prioritize resident allocation for KV buffers for hot models on Dedicated/Private (doc changes + autosizer). Low code risk.
2) Add a soft-page-prefetch step before fusion handoff: small pre-warm (touch key pages) with minimal runtime toggles. Medium code risk.
3) Fusion-aware prefetch policy: when fusing, prefetch the pages required by the fused kernel path. Medium-high risk (changes kernel scheduling).
4) Coalescer adaptive policy: use telemetry to detect page-in frequency and relax sleep time proactively. Medium risk.
5) Fallback: expose a runtime flag to disable fusion for models with high paging. Low risk but hurts median latency.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Is paging source NVMe reads (model shards) or GPU page faults from unified memory/driver? Need to confirm with low-level driver traces and strace on the server.
- Can we reproduce the phenomenon deterministically by injecting a synthetic page-in event? If yes, measure critical section size threshold where spike occurs.
- Evaluate prefetch-touch overhead: how many ms does it add per-token and does it reduce spike amplitude enough to be worth it?
- Test in mixed workload (short chat + long-doc summarization concurrently) to check if mixture increases pulse amplitude.

Repro plan for deeper root-cause (next 2 weeks):
- Week 1: deterministic injection harness + synthetic page-throb tool. Target: produce a controlled page-in at T=30s and measure kernel reaction. Owner: Aisha Khan.
- Week 2: implement minimal prefetch-touch in runtime (feature-flagged). Run A/B: prefetch on vs off across 6 rigs. Owner: Miguel Torres.
- Week 3: telem patch to coalescer to log page-in metrics + decision surface; evaluate on Dedicated canary. Owner: Samir Patel.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is sketchy; it's a working lab diary. Expect half-formed ideas. Please add your trace snippets, especially if you see different cadence than 120s.
- If you have access to kernels with unified memory page-fault counters (driver trace), paste a sample into /confluence/serving-runtime/steady-state-probing for cross-team visibility.

Raw numbers appendix (sample run):
- run-id: run-20250212-01
- median: 6.9 ms
- p90: 11.7 ms
- p95: 12.8 ms
- p99: 27.6 ms
- periodicity: ~115–130 s
- avg page-ins per minute (host): 0.8

Quick wins for product teams:
- On Dedicated, recommend reservation of extra GPU memory margin in capacity planner to keep popular models resident. Add a note to Dedicated onboarding docs.
- For hosted tier, add telemetry to surface model-specific p99 cadence that could indicate paging problems to SRE.
